svg.title: TOPAK D6 — A workflow may be a mesh: a budget makes it end, the activation is the unit, and the mechanism is the bus
svg.desc: ADR-0055 (Proposed 2026.10.07, at R2) widens ADR-0054 (Proposed; its DAG is drawn in C9). A workflow declares its kind; a mesh may have cycles and does not load without an activation budget the promotion votes on, every lease charged to it, the orchestrator's rounds included. A node may run more than once, so the unit of attributes, routes and findings becomes the activation, with its causal history. The mechanism tracks the work and the orchestrator keeps nothing between rounds; the events a mesh reacts to are entries in the consensus log. Nothing here is in force: spec/Mesh.tla is checked by TLC and has no proof, and the reference follows the record under ADR-0033 A16, pending, on a floor stage that is not in force (G11 §1.1, §3, §7 items 101, 102; ToO rev 15 §2.11).
svg.text: TOPAK · D6

text.tspan: A workflow may be a mesh: a budget makes it end, the activation is the unit, and the mechanism is the bus

svg.text: ADR-0055 (Proposed 2026.10.07, at R2) widens ADR-0054 (Proposed; its DAG is drawn in C9). A workflow declares its kind; a mesh may have cycles and does not load without an activation budget the promotion votes on, every lease charged to it, the orchestrator's rounds included. A node may run more than once, so the unit of attributes, routes and findings becomes the activation, with its causal history. The mechanism tracks

the work and the orchestrator keeps nothing between rounds; the events a mesh reacts to are entries in the consensus log. Nothing here is in force: spec/Mesh.tla is checked by TLC and has no proof, and the reference follows the record under ADR-0033 A16, pending, on a floor stage that is not in force (G11 §1.1, §3, §7 items 101, 102; ToO rev 15 §2.11).

text.tspan: Proposed · R8; the 2-colour entry not drafted
Built at reference · in part · on a floor stage not in force
fan-out joins, pools, parity seatings, T_wf, the gate's evidence

svg.text: Every clause subtracts except the budgeted grant, whose authority is the promotion's, as in ADR-0054; confirmation is required under C1 because the grant path now issues leases out of a budget (status note). One author, one day: drafted 2026.10.07 from a design discussion in which the custodian settled five things, ⟨M1⟩ to ⟨M5⟩ (a mesh, not only a DAG; promoted to Run and run by the mechanism; workers of alternate lineage; the orchestrator tracks and routes as
needed; a record of its own beside ADR-0054). Every other choice is the drafter's, and not reviewed by a reader other than the drafter (§11; ADR-0029 A2).

One unit is one cell-round: a worker's or the orchestrator's lease, with its cell Observer's, which rides with its cell and is not charged separately (drafter's choice). The orchestrator's rounds are charged: under M_ORCHFREE they are not, and BudgetBound breaks (row of1). Had (s,1) and (s,2) both ended bad, the loop would turn twice and (w,
2) take unit 6; (s, 3) would then be ready, its grant refused, and the workflow failed, never completed.

text.tspan: Four other runs of the same mesh, each a witness TLC reached (§11;

svg.text: Ordered after (s, 2) began, against the worker's round. (s, 2) is clean, and every edge out of it is disabled, because the finding is in its causal history (§3).
A route decided before the finding is void at apply, history: witness NeverVoidedByHistory (w_voidhistory).
M_SOURCEONLY, a finding closing only its own activation, breaks NoActivationAfterFinding (so1).
Its label is its clearSet, which only grows. e3 is clear, so (s, 2) is labelled untrusted: NeverTaintAroundLoop (w_taintloop).
e2 enters the outward sink, so the routing rule disables it for the rest of the run; the workflow fails: NeverExitClosedByTaint (w_exitclosed).
M_FORGETTAINT breaks LabelCoversTruth and TaintedNeverOutward (ft1, ft2).
The route names its activation and its round, so it is void at apply, lease: the stale route, witness NeverVoidedByLease (w_voidlease).
A lapsed round fails its event and takes no default edge (§6; ADR-0054 §8).
M_TRACKER, one lease across events and a route that names its node, breaks RouteOnItsEvent (tr1).
(s,1), round 1, (w,1), (s,2), round 2, (w,2): six units. (s, 3) is ready and its grant is refused: NeverExhausted (w_exhausted).
Running out of budget fails the workflow, never completes it, as a timeout never grants (ADR-0024 §2).
M_BUDGETDONE breaks CompletedOnlyBySink (bd1). The loop running and completing after a loop: w_looped, w_completedloop.

text.tspan: One run of it, as activations in log order, each with its trigger and causal history (§3) · Proposed
§2 · The promotion votes on a budget, and the budget is what makes a mesh end
A budgeted mesh is a DAG unrolled to depth

svg.text: unit 1
unit 2
unit 3
unit 4
unit 5
unit 6
refused
event

unit 3: completes
unit 6: completes

Its behaviours are exactly those of the mesh unrolled to depth N, so ADR-0054's safety argument holds per activation; the mesh adds compactness and an iteration count decided at run time within the bound (§2). Drawn here from

Mesh.tla's Grant and OrchGrant, as an illustration: this set of reachable activations is what the gate would show the quorum, and the gate's evidence is not built (I49). The cost falls on the reviewers, who approve every unrolling at
once.
The leases the workflow may ever issue: workers' and the orchestrator's. The promotion grants at most
None yet: an open obligation, "as placeholders
first"
Charged on every grant; a refusal fails the slot
Optional, per node
None yet
Not named in A16 or I49; workflow.rs's Budget carries
Wall-clock for the whole workflow; ADR-0054 §1 already has it
None yet; a placeholder and a deployment's
Not built: no replicated clock

The quorum votes on the budget with the graph and the seatings. Without one, the promotion would be a standing grant of unbounded leases, which "promotion is a grant" cannot mean. A time bound alone bounds wall-clock, not leases, and would make
termination a liveness property needing fairness (Options).

text.tspan: A grant the budget cannot pay is refused

svg.text: The activation fails, and running out of budget fails the workflow, never completes it, as a timeout never grants
A refused grant is never granted lower, and no other seating stands in (ADR-0054 §2).

text.tspan: "It ends" stays a bounded safety property

svg.text: Every behaviour of a budgeted mesh issues at most N leases, so a model checker decides termination at small N, and
no property needs fairness (§2; Consequences).
That is what ADR-0054's DAG had from its shape (Context).

text.tspan: The budget must charge the orchestrator (finding 2)

svg.text: A bound on worker leases alone leaves the one cell that runs at every decision unbounded.
The runs said it a second way: uncharged, or charged once, the orchestrator frees worker rounds: 2.1 million states against more than 280 million (R1; G11 §3, result 10).

text.tspan: The gate computes, as evidence for the vote

svg.text: The activations the mesh can reach within N, and every edge whose guard is identically true (drafter's choice). Neither refuses; both say what is being voted on.
It refuses a mesh without a budget, and one whose clear edges cannot be 2-coloured (§11).
Not built (I49); how the set is shown, and at what size it stops being readable, is open.

text.tspan: §3, §4 · The activation is the unit of attributes, routes and findings; joins are scoped to a fan-out

svg.text: Acyclic, checked at load; a dag with a cycle does not load (§1)
May have cycles, self-loops included; does not load without a budget (§1). dag stays the default, and a deployment may refuse the kind in its bundle's load check
Its shape: a checker reaches every path, and no liveness argument is needed (Context)
The budget: at most N leases, so "it ends" is a bounded safety property (§2)
A node is one round of one cell (§1)
An activation, a pair (node, k), one round of one cell; a node may run more than once (§3)
Lifted once when a node's round ends; found alone changes after, false to true (§4)
Per activation, written once; found as before (§3)
Every activation records its trigger: the activation it was entered from, or the fan-out it belongs to. Its causal history is itself and its trigger's history; the log holds both, so the
history is a fact (§3)
The source and the nodes that dominate it, all ended before the source is ready (§4)
The triggering activation and its causal history, never a node's latest value, which can change between decide and apply when the node runs again. BasisStable carries over;
Mesh.tla does not restate it (§3; finding 3)
A decision point, consumed once by one route (§8)
A decision event, the activation's end, consumed by one route. An older event stays routable until it is consumed, fails, or a finding closes it (§3)
The decision point, with its basis (§8)
Its activation and its round: void at apply if the activation's event was consumed or failed, or the round has moved on (§3, §6)
Edges out of its source or any ancestor (§8)
Every edge out of an activation with the finding anywhere in its causal history. On a loop, a finding against the worker's round stops the route out of the decision node's next
round, though that round is clean (§3)
Each branch runs at most once (Context)
One live activation per node (drafter's choice): a seating names one principal, which holds one live lease (ADR-0031 §2). To run concurrently a node names a pool of seatings,
each charged when used (§3)
Waits for its predecessors; one that can no longer fire is skipped (§1)
Waits for the branches of one fan-out activation, matched by its identity, which every branch carries as its trigger; the skip is scoped the same way. any is unchanged (§4)
Thinkers alternate on every clear edge, at the tally (§6)
The clear edges form a 2-colourable graph under two lineages (§5)
Every sink ended or skipped, and at least one ended (§9)
An activation of a sink has ended (§8)
spec/Workflow.tla, 33 rows (G11 §3)
spec/Mesh.tla, 23 rows. ADR-0054's one-decision properties are Workflow.tla's and are not repeated

text.tspan: What a mesh inherits from ADR-0054 unchanged (drawn in C9)

svg.text: The promotion grants every lease: a third grant path, the only clause that adds authority, and none the
quorum did not vote on. No principal grants another (ADR-0054 §2).
The orchestrator only narrows: it selects among edges whose guards hold, with Route(edge) and Report,
and is delivered handles and never bytes (§3).
A route is checked again where it is applied, and void if it fails; a lapsed orchestrator takes no default edge
Labels cross cells along the edges: an input labelled by the reporter's clearSet, and the routing rule over
labels (§5). An edge waits for its source's coverage (§7).
Read per activation where ADR-0055 says so (§1).
The interpreter of ADR-0054 §11 gains activation records, causal histories, a budget counter and the
orchestrator's track, under the same mechanism row of ADR-0045: every decision they make subtracts or
executes a grant the quorum made, and the budget bounds the grant.
The mechanism grows again, on the path every Run grant travels (Consequences).

It does not pass the tally. A workflow fixes it by making one edge of the cycle a handle edge, which carries no bytes
into its target. A third lineage is allowed where a deployment has one, and not required (Options).

The node gets two seatings of different lineages, used by activation parity (drafter's choice: both fixes are allowed).
Parity seatings are not in the module and are not built (§11; I49).

text.tspan: Taint on a loop only grows (finding 5)

svg.text: clean
reads untrusted
untrusted
untrusted
disabled for the rest of the run
An input's label is its reporter's clearSet, and a clearSet only grows, so once untrusted content is read on a clear
cycle, every later activation on it is labelled untrusted and the routing rule closes the cycle's outward edges for the
rest of the run. Taint cannot be laundered round a loop.
Over the graph and the seatings, at the promotion tally, where a refusal stalls (§5; ADR-0035 §5 R8, which already
says a workflow whose clear edges are not bipartite cannot meet the rule).
ADR-0035 is Proposed, so it is declared, not enforced (ADR-0054 D-0054-1). ADR-0055's entry in ADR-0035 §5 is
not drafted (§11).

text.tspan: A cycle repeats what alternation cannot stop

svg.text: Alternation keeps a trigger from crossing one clear hop into its own lineage. It does not stop it reaching that lineage

text.tspan: again two hops on, and a loop offers that every turn.

svg.text: Labels are what bound it (§5): the two-hop gap is bounded because taint only grows (finding 5).
An honest loop that reads untrusted content once loses its outward reach for good: ADR-0054's finding 6, made
stronger (Consequences). "That is the right direction to fail" (§5).
Two lineages constrain the graph further: an odd clear cycle needs a handle edge or parity seatings.

text.tspan: Built at reference · in part · A16 pending

svg.text: Lineage is a tag the text declares, compared on every clear edge at load; a clear edge with one declared lineage
on both ends does not load. No independence table exists (G18).
A clear input's label joins the receiver's clearSet at grant; an edge into an outward node is disabled by an untrusted
attribute (untrusted_content_read_on_the_loop_disables_the_exit).

text.tspan: §6, §7 · The mechanism tracks; the orchestrator holds no state; event-driven means the mechanism is the bus

input (ADR-0043 §1).
Its round ends on its outcome: the end and its attributes are one log entry.
Never addressed by w. No variant publishes to another cell or subscribes to anything
A round topic is read only by the seats in its watched-by relation.
One round per decision event, granted from the budget when the event opens;
ended when its route applies or its lease lapses. Events are served in log order
(drafter's choice).
It keeps nothing between rounds. It emits Route(edge) naming its activation and
its round.

not supported

The consensus log: the events a mesh reacts to are entries in it (§7), each applied by every replica at its position

text.tspan: In the same apply, the mechanism evaluates what each entry enables

svg.text: What an entry enables, in the same apply (§7): the attributes lifted, a computed edge (e3) evaluated, a decision event opened, every edge downstream of a finding closed, a committed route checked again and voided if it fails (§3).
Every grant is charged to the budget or refused (§2): a ready activation's lease, and the orchestrator's round for an event that has opened (§6).
It holds the track: activations, their triggers and causal histories, the budget counter. The log holds both trigger and history, so the history is a fact (§3, §10).

text.tspan: Kafka: round topics carry the records and order nothing (ADR-0005)

svg.text: Kafka is neither the ordering authority nor the system of record: the causal frame is the Paxos log, and Kafka's guarantee is durability in the window (ADR-0005, R1). The delivered track is written to the orchestrator's round topic as the round's opening record, as ADR-0048 §2 does for the tool list, so its Observer
reads what the orchestrator was given (§6).
its end, its Reports
a lease the promotion grants
the track: typed facts,
labels, triggers, handles;
never bytes
Route(edge):
activation + round
records carried, unordered

text.tspan: Orchestration over a log: ADR-0054's shape, with cycles (Context) · Proposed
"The orchestrator tracks" is met by the mechanism (§6) ⟨M4⟩
The orchestrator keeps nothing between rounds. Three reasons, each sufficient:

svg.text: A lease is round-coterminous and lasts at most T_persona (ADR-0031 §2, A2). A long mesh outlives any one lease, so a tracking orchestrator would need
successor grants inside the workflow, which ADR-0054 §2 excludes.
State carried across rounds is persistent agent memory, which the corpus puts outside the pattern.
A long-lived orchestrator makes routes ambiguous: a route decided on one event and committed after the next has opened would land on the wrong activation
unless it names its own.
One lease across decision events, and a route that names its node, not its activation: it applies to whichever activation of the node is open when it commits.
RouteOnItsEvent breaks (tr1).
A route here names both its activation and its round; the module does not show which alone suffices (finding 4).

text.tspan: Why choreography is not supported (§7; Options; finding 6)

svg.text: In choreography workers publish events and others subscribe, and no one decides what runs next. Rejected: no variant subscribes, a round topic is read only by
its watchers, and no component that is not a model would decide what runs next.
Every reading in which cells react to each other directly puts a model's output in charge of what runs next. Event-driven and havoc are compatible only with the

text.tspan: Consequences the record states against itself

svg.text: Budget burning. A Byzantine worker that always reports retry, or an orchestrator that always loops, spends the budget and fails the workflow. Safe, and paid for in
principals. A correlation over it is owed to ADR-0051 (Open obligations; G11 item 97).
Many principals: two per activation and two per orchestrator round, up to N of each kind of round.
Reviewers approve every unrolling at once. The gate's evidence helps; it does not make a large mesh easy to read.
Positive: loops whose length is decided at run time, inside a bound the quorum voted on; ADR-0054's safety argument carries over per activation; no principal
seats another, and the budget bounds how many seatings a promotion can produce; the orchestrator is stateless and still informed.
An activation of a sink has ended. Completion still says the graph was traversed, and nothing about whether the work is right
The budget refuses a grant: running out never completes it
§2, §8; M_BUDGETDONE
T_wf passes: a timeout is always a failure
It is quiescent: no activation ready or running, no decision event open, no route in flight, and no sink ended
§8; Mesh.tla Quiescent
ADR-0054 §9's other failures, per activation: a node fails, a decision event fails, a grant is refused, the epoch is fenced
A workflow's failure stops nothing else: every cell's lease ends by its own path (ADR-0054 §9). Mesh.tla does not check deadlock: a workflow may stall, and stalling is safe (header).
None of its own. ADR-0054's two apply per activation: D-0054-1, lineage alternation declared and not enforced, every deployment today; D-0054-2, coverage at the edge waived (ADR-0054 §10).

A deployment that runs only dag workflows is not degenerate on this record; it has not taken the widening (§9). One that wants only DAGs refuses the kind in its bundle's load check (§1), which the reference does not build (I49).

A violated row's state count is TLC's when it stopped at the first counterexample, with states still queued. "The other six" are the seven properties less the one the mutation is about. Runner mesh-gen-results.sh; TLC 2.19 (the
results file's header).
CapOnePast == nAll <= N + 1: one lease past the budget, the reach M_OVERRUN's row has with no constraint. Used by of_rest and tr_rest and no other
row, by the custodian's decision (R1; G11 §5: a remainder with no bound is checked under a stated cap, and the cap is a row).
Under either mutation the budget buys more worker rounds, and the state space outgrows the machine.
Unconstrained, M_ORCHFREE had reached 282 million states with 125 million still queued after eight hours, and was stopped (§11).
"The runs say finding 2 a second way": an uncharged orchestrator, or one charged once for the run, frees worker rounds, the difference between 2.1 million
states and more than 280 million (R1).
Fan-out, scoped joins and serialisation per node (the mesh never runs two activations at once); pools; a self-loop with parity seatings.
Observer lineage; epochs and fences; the track the orchestrator is delivered; the gate's bipartite check, which is static, and whose runtime consequence is
ClearHopsAlternate.
Proofs. Deadlock is not checked.

text.tspan: At the reference: ADR-0033 A16, pending, on the
floor stage, which is not in force

svg.text: §11's reference item is met in part ⟨R2⟩: the reference at 11aaf6a (SHA256SUMS-REF-2026.10.08). One engine runs both kinds: each node run is an activation with its trigger and causal history, and a dag is the case of one activation per node (I49). The reference links a floor that is not in force, at the custodian's direction (G11 item 102). It discharges nothing in force: on ADR-0055's ratification, every behaviour of §11 is seen, at the replicated state and not end to end (A16).

text.tspan: Test at the replicated state, named after

svg.text: The loop turns twice and exits
The budget refuses a grant and the workflow fails
An orchestrator round is charged
A finding against the worker's round voids the decision node's next route
A route decided in one round and committed after it ends is void
Untrusted content read on the loop disables the exit
A mesh loads only with a budget and two-coloured clear edges

The last row is A16's load check (ADR-0055 §1), not one of §11's six. spec/Mesh.tla is tied to the reference by tests named after its properties and by no trace: spec/Mechanism.tla does not model workflows, and trace validation was not rerun. mechanism/lean is stale, by the custodian's
decision of 2026.10.08 (A16).

text.tspan: Not met, and not built (§11; A16; I49)

svg.text: No mesh is run end to end, and the cells are the tests': a test drives each session, a BOOTSTRAP standing in for a launch per slot (I49 (g)).
Fan-out-scoped joins, pools and parity seatings are not built: a mesh with an all join does not load (I49 (d), PROVISIONAL workflow-mesh-joins).
Not built: T_wf and the step bound (no replicated clock); the gate's evidence for a mesh's vote (reachable activations within N); the bundle's refusal of a kind; seatings above rung 0.
A finding has a form the reference chose (I49 (a), PROVISIONAL finding-record), and only workflows read it.
A clear input is delivered only by the replica that holds the predecessor's reports (I49 (f); mechanism/ finding 23).

text.tspan: ADR-0055's tables, findings and obligations, in full

svg.text: ADR-0054 is ratified first, or with this record
Not met. ADR-0054 is Proposed (G11 §1.1)
The dependent entries are drafted: ADR-0054 §1, §2, §4, §8 and §9, read per activation and with the
kind and the budget; ADR-0035 §5 (the 2-colour check)
Not met. "ADR-0055's dependent entries are not drafted" (G11 §1.1). The twelve amendments pending are ADR-0054's ten, A16 and A17
A module states the properties and its mutations break them, by ADR-0046's method
Met for TLC at drafting ⟨R1⟩, with two remainders bounded. Not met: fan-out, scoped joins and pools; serialisation per node; a self-loop with
parity seatings; the static 2-colour check, which belongs to the gate; proofs (G11 item 101)
The gate computes the reachable activations within N and the edges with identically true guards, as
evidence; refuses a mesh without a budget, and one whose clear edges cannot be 2-coloured
Not met. The evidence is not built (I49). At the reference's load, a mesh with no budget and a clear edge with one declared lineage at both ends
do not load (A16)
The reference, with an ADR-0033 addendum: the module's mesh run by scripted cells, six behaviours
each seen
Met in part ⟨R2⟩: A16, pending. Every behaviour seen at the replicated state; no mesh run end to end
A reader who is not the drafter (ADR-0029 A2)
A budgeted mesh is a DAG unrolled to depth N. The budget is not an add-on to the mesh; it is what lets the DAG's argument apply to it at all
The budget must charge the orchestrator. A bound on worker leases alone leaves the one cell that runs at every decision unbounded (G11 §3, result 10)
The DAG's settled guards were a property of dominators, and dominators do not survive a cycle. Causal history is what does: the activations that led to this one, recorded by the log and immutable

"The orchestrator tracks" pulls toward a long lease, and a long lease is three problems at once: T_persona, memory across rounds, and routes that land on the wrong activation. Moving the tracking into the mechanism solves all
three. M_TRACKER removes both the activation and the round from a route, and the module does not show which alone suffices
Taint on a loop only grows. Labels from clearSet make that automatic. It is the reason alternation's two-hop gap on a cycle is bounded, and the reason honest loops will find their exits closed
Event-driven and havoc are compatible only with the mechanism as the bus. Every reading in which cells react to each other directly puts a model's output in charge of what runs next
Not taken ⟨M5⟩. The DAG stays the default and the simpler record; the mesh is a widening a deployment opts into
Choreography: cells publish events and subscribe to each other's
Rejected. No variant subscribes, a round topic is read only by its watchers, and no component that is not a model would decide what runs next
Cycles with no budget, bounded by T_wf alone
Rejected. A time bound bounds wall-clock, not leases; the promotion would be a grant of as many leases as fit in T_wf, and termination would
become a liveness property needing fairness
Rejected. The orchestrator's rounds would be unbounded. M_ORCHFREE
Unroll every loop into a DAG, as ADR-0054 requires
Kept as the default. The mesh is the same behaviours without the unrolling, and the gate's reachable-activation set restores what unrolling showed

text.tspan: Guards that read a node's latest attributes

svg.text: Rejected. Not settled: a node that runs again changes them between decide and apply

text.tspan: A finding that closes only its own activation

svg.text: Rejected. A loop routes round a finding one hop downstream. M_SOURCEONLY
A tracking orchestrator with one long lease ⟨M4⟩ as first read
Not taken. It outlives T_persona, carries memory across rounds, and makes routes ambiguous (§6). M_TRACKER. The tracking is kept, in the
mechanism
Rejected by ADR-0031 §2. A pool of seatings is the way (§3)

text.tspan: Alternation by a third lineage on odd cycles

svg.text: Not required. It is allowed where a deployment has one; with two, a handle edge or parity seatings fix the cycle (§5)
Rejected. Not well defined when a branch can run more than once
Not taken (drafter's choice). They ride with their cell; a deployment that wants principal counts multiplies by two
Initial draft. A workflow declares its kind, and a mesh may have cycles under an activation budget the promotion votes on, the
orchestrator's rounds charged to it; the activation is the unit of attributes, routes and findings, with guards over causal history; one
live activation per node; scoped joins; a 2-colourable clear graph; the mechanism tracks and the orchestrator holds no state, one
round per decision event; the mechanism is the bus; completion and failure; no degeneracy of its own
The custodian's decisions ⟨M1⟩ to ⟨M5⟩,
2026.10.07; the sources in the provenance note

each break their property and nothing else. The remainder rows for M_ORCHFREE and M_TRACKER are checked under CapOnePast
, one lease past the budget, by the custodian's decision; unconstrained they outgrow the machine. The runs say finding 2 a
second way. No decision text changes
